anatomy.intro: Silver spoons combines finely hairy leaves with short leaf stalks and branching stems.

parts.function: Dense hairs and a waxy coating give the leaf its pale appearance.
parts.label: Silver surface

parts.function: The thick leaf supplies both photosynthetic area and water storage.
parts.label: Spoon-shaped blade

parts.function: A short stalk attaches the blade to the stem.
parts.label: Short petiole

parts.function: Somewhat woody stems support the spreading crown of opposite leaves.
parts.label: Branching stem

flowers.text: The species bears red tubular flowers in clusters at the branch ends. A clear flowering photograph would add a useful identifying feature to the current foliage evidence.

growth.note: Slow growth is typical; the exact species remains probable until stronger identifying evidence is available.

stages.text: Young shoots add paired leaves at their tips.
stages.title: Open leaf pairs

stages.text: An erect shoot develops a broader, mounding outline.
stages.title: Branch outward

stages.text: Mature shoot tips may develop a branched inflorescence.
stages.title: Form flower clusters

habitat.text: Kalanchoe bracteata is native to Madagascar, with Kew placing it in a seasonally dry tropical biome. It grows as a small succulent shrub rather than a ground-hugging rosette. The silver plant in this collection remains a probable match; that distinction matters because several related kalanchoes share pale, hairy foliage.

lookalikes.name: Copper spoons (Kalanchoe orgyalis)
lookalikes.text: Copper spoons has cinnamon-colored upper leaf felt and greyer undersides. This probable silver-spoons plant has a predominantly silver to olive appearance; color alone does not settle every Kalanchoe identification.

mature.text: NC State describes shrubs about 2–4 ft tall and similarly wide. That describes mature horticultural potential, not a target for this shared box. Leaving space between its crown and lower rosette neighbors helps keep the planting readable and evenly lit.

milestones.text: Acquired at Gerych's Greenhouse in the shared P20 / #2 succulent planter.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

nameStory.text: Bracteata refers to floral bracts. The familiar 'silver spoons' name instead describes the silvery, spoon-shaped leaves visitors can recognize before it flowers.
